text: Kann ich mein Gepäck hier lassen?
ipa: kˌan ɪç maɪn ɡəpˈɛk hˈiːɾ lˈasən

text: Kann ich noch eine Nacht bleiben?
ipa: kˌan ɪç nɔx ˌaɪnə nˈaxt blˈaɪbən

text: Es gibt ein Problem mit dem Zimmer.
ipa: ɛs ɡˈiːpt aɪn pɾoːblˈeːm mɪt deːm tsˈɪmɜ

text: Bitte schicken Sie jemanden zum Reparieren.
ipa: bˈɪtə ʃˈɪkən ziː jˈeːmandən tsʊm rˌeːparˈiːrən

literal: please stop -- aufhören is lexically terminal against unterbrechen and Pause, so German needs no second clause where the Mandarin row carries one; two words and unsoftened, against this pack's usual Können Sie ...? / Ich möchte ... padding
a short break, please -- Pause says temporarily on its own, which is the whole distinction from the row above
please do not massage this spot -- Stelle is the noun German contraindication guidance uses for a spot that has to be left out (die betroffene Stelle sollte nicht massiert werden)

please a little firmer -- fest, not stark, is the trade's pressure word: a German massage school's own guidance quotes clients asking ruhig fester and richtig fest and warns against the question Zu fest?. Three words beginning Bitte against the two of Sanfter, bitte, because neither button carries a labelKey on the spa board and the owner's own wording is what labels them, side by side
gentler, please -- sanft is the bottom of the same school's sanft / mittel / kräftig pressure scale, so it is about pressure and not speed

text: Der Druck ist genau richtig, bitte so weiter.
ipa: dɛɾ dɾˈʊk ɪst ɡənˈaʊ rˈɪçtɪç, bˈɪtə zoː vˈaɪtɜ
literal: the pressure is exactly right, please carry on like that -- a confirmation with a keep-it-there clause, not praise; Druck is the trade's noun for what is being confirmed

text: Bitte vor allem die Schultern massieren.
ipa: bˈɪtə fˌɔɾ ˈaləm diː ʃˈʊltɜn masˈiːrən

text: Bitte vor allem den Rücken massieren.
ipa: bˈɪtə fˌɔɾ ˈaləm deːn rˈykən masˈiːrən

text: Bitte vor allem den Nacken massieren.
ipa: bˈɪtə fˌɔɾ ˈaləm deːn nˈakən masˈiːrən
literal: Nacken is Duden's hinterer Teil des Halses, the back of the neck, and is the massage word; Hals is the neck as a whole including the throat and would be wrong here. The trade groups this with the shoulders as the Nacken-Schulter-Bereich and sells Schulter-Nacken-Massage as one service, but the two rows stay separate because a board button is one meaning

text: Bitte vor allem die Füße massieren.
ipa: bˈɪtə fˌɔɾ ˈaləm diː fˈyːsə masˈiːrən
literal: Fußmassage and Fußreflexzonenmassage are bookable services of their own in German-speaking spas, so this reads as asking for one rather than for part of a full-body treatment

text: Gut, ich lasse die Stelle aus.
ipa: ɡˈuːt, ɪç lˈasə diː ʃtˈɛlə ˈaʊs
literal: all right, I will leave that spot out -- 1sg present, which carries no gender in German

text: Diese Behandlung geht nicht ohne diese Stelle.
ipa: dˌiːzə bəhˈandlʊŋ ɡˈeːt nˈɪçt ˈoːnə dˌiːzə ʃtˈɛlə
literal: this treatment does not work without that spot -- Behandlung is one bookable treatment, not a Kur, which would be a course of several and overstate what is being refused

text: Ich bin nicht sicher, ich frage bei der Leitung nach.
ipa: ɪç bɪn nˈɪçt zˈɪçɜ, ɪç frˈɑːɡə baɪ dɛɾ lˈaɪtʊŋ nˈɑːx
literal: I am not sure, I will check with the management -- die Leitung is an abstract role noun, so it names the supervisor without choosing Chef or Chefin; sicher is predicative and German predicative adjectives do not inflect, so the speaker is not gendered either
